methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion is a Series G robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The comparable universe in Robotics & Manufacturing comprises nine private peers (including Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics) and one public company, though a sufficiently tight peer set at identical stage and valuation tier does not exist to support median multiples analysis.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($150M) as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement yields an implied valuation of $188M. This single-method result forms the median of the triangulated range.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $159M (low) to $216M (high), with $188M as the central point. The range reflects sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier assumption. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight comparable transactions at Distalmotion's stage, which limits external validation of the 1.25x step multiplier, and incomplete visibility into Distalmotion's specific financial performance relative to the broader peer set. Any refinement to this valuation would require additional comparable data at Series G in robotics or clarification of the company's revenue, unit economics, or path to profitability relative to identified peers.
